|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `SPLIT_ALWAYS` | A5 + B1 | B12 | B6 | 5 | 19 | **1** | 24 ✓ |
| `SINGLE_PREFERRED` *(default)* | B6 | B12 | A5 + B1 | 5 | 19 | **1** | 24 ✓ |
| `SINGLE_STRICT` | B6 | B12 | **A5 only** | 5 | 18 | 0 | **23 ✗ (1 pc lost)** |

`SPLIT_ALWAYS` and `SINGLE_PREFERRED` produce **identical RDC totals** — only *which* line carries
the split moves, and `SINGLE_PREFERRED` pushes it to the lowest-ranked store.
`SINGLE_STRICT` avoids splits at the cost of reducing an allocated line (§B6.3).

### E3 — SHIP + HOLD on one ledger (D2)

TBL option, size M, stock **A = 3, B = 9** (clubbed 12). Allocation: HS11 (own A) ship 5 + hold 2;
HP04 (own B) ship 4 + hold 1.

| # | Store | Draw | Qty | A bal | B bal | From A | From B | A after | B after |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | HS11 | SHIP | 5 | 3 | 9 | **3** | **2** | 0 | 7 |
| 2 | HS11 | HOLD | 2 | 0 | 7 | 0 | **2** | 0 | 5 |
| 3 | HP04 | SHIP | 4 | 0 | 5 | — | **4** | 0 | 1 |
| 4 | HP04 | HOLD | 1 | 0 | 1 | — | **1** | 0 | 0 |
| | | | **12** | | | **3** | **9** | ✓ | ✓ |

Hold tracking records HS11 → 2 pcs at **B**, HP04 → 1 pc at **B**. Next run those pieces are
already netted out of B's pool and each store's `RL_HOLD_QTY` releases correctly.

**Two failure modes this prevents:**

| Wrong approach | What breaks |
|---|---|
| Hold tagged to the store's own RDC regardless of stock | HS11's 2 pcs tagged to A, which has 0 left → **phantom hold**; next run deducts stock that was never reserved and HS11 waits forever |
| SHIP and HOLD tagged in two independent passes | Both see B = 9 and together book 12 from B → **double-booked stock** |

### E4 — Mixed store master (D3, Option A)

**Store master** (deliberately messy)

| Store | `ST_MASTER.RDC` | Tier used |
|---|---|---|
| HS11 | `RDC-A` | 1 — own |
| HS12 | *(blank)* | 2 — global `"A,B"` |
| HP04 | `RDC-B` | 1 — own |
| HP09 | `ALL` | 2 — global `"A,B"` |

**Stock, L-size:** A = 15, B = 20 → clubbed 35. Allocation from the clubbed pool — **the tag is
not read**, so every store is served:

| Store | Allocated | Today's result |
|---|---|---|
| HS11 | 10 | 10 |
| HS12 | **12** | **0** — blank tag matches no pool key |
| HP04 | 4 | 4 |
| HP09 | **3** | **0** — `'ALL'` is not a real RDC code |
| | **29** | 14 |

**Split pass** (`SINGLE_PREFERRED`, `ALC_RDC_PRIORITY = "A,B"`)

| # | Store | Tier / preference | Need | A bal | B bal | Covered by | From A | From B | A after | B after |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | HS11 | 1 — own `A` | 10 | 15 | 20 | A | **10** | — | 5 | 20 |
| 2 | HS12 | 2 — `A,B` | 12 | 5 | 20 | B | — | **12** | 5 | 8 |
| 3 | HP04 | 1 — own `B` | 4 | 5 | 8 | B | — | **4** | 5 | 4 |
| 4 | HP09 | 2 — `A,B` | 3 | 5 | 4 | **both** | **3** | — | 2 | 4 |
| | | | **29** | | | | **13** | **16** | | |

**Where the tier actually matters.** Only line 4 — both warehouses could serve it:

| If HP09's preference came from | Ships from | Store receives |
|---|---|---|
| tier 1, a real tag `RDC-B` | B | 3 |
| tier 2, `ALC_RDC_PRIORITY = "A,B"` | A | 3 |
| tier 2, `ALC_RDC_PRIORITY = "B,A"` | B | 3 |
| tier 3, largest-available | A (5 > 4) | 3 |

Lines 1-3 were decided by **availability**, not preference. **An untagged store never loses
stock — it only loses the ability to state a preference, and only on lines where both warehouses
could have served it.**

## B11. Invariants

| ID | Invariant | Enforcement |
|---|---|---|
| I-1 | `Σ ARS_ALLOC_RDC_SPLIT.SHIP_QTY = Σ ARS_ALLOC_WORKING.SHIP_QTY` (per session) | assertion in the pass + test V4 |
| I-2 | `Σ ARS_ALLOC_RDC_SPLIT.HOLD_QTY = Σ ARS_ALLOC_WORKING.HOLD_QTY` | same |
| I-3 | Per `(SRC_RDC, option, size)`: `Σ (SHIP_QTY + HOLD_QTY) ≤ that RDC's MSA FNL_Q` | ledger can never go negative; test V3 |
| I-4 | Every allocation line with `SHIP_QTY > 0` has ≥ 1 split row | test |
| I-5 | `Own` / `Cross` output is byte-identical to the pre-change build | regression diff V5 — **release gate** |
| I-6 | The pass is deterministic: same inputs → same `SRC_RDC` assignment | fixed ordering; test re-run |

Exception to I-1: `SINGLE_STRICT` reduces `ARS_ALLOC_WORKING.SHIP_QTY` **before** the comparison,
so the invariant still holds post-pass.

## B12. Edge cases

| Case | Handling |
|---|---|
| Store tag names an RDC with no stock for the option | Tier 1 finds nothing; walk proceeds to the next RDC. No special code |
| Option exists at only one RDC | Every line sources there; no splits possible |
| `SHIP_QTY = 0`, `HOLD_QTY > 0` | Hold is tagged normally; no ship row emitted |
| Line reduced to 0 under `SINGLE_STRICT` | Row stays with `SHIP_QTY = 0` and remark `RDC_SINGLE_SHORT`; treated as not-allocated by Part 8.5 |
| Part 8.55 releases a hold after tagging | Hold released on the working / parked / split rows alike; the pieces stay unallocated in the RDC that held them |
| Three or more RDCs in future | The pass is written for **N** RDCs; the preference order simply grows. No two-RDC assumption anywhere |
| Rounding | The pass moves whole allocated pieces only — it never re-derives a quantity, so pack-size rounding done in the engine is preserved exactly |

Final document delivered in both formats:

**[2026-09-19-central-rdc-pool-allocation-brd-fsd.md](docs/superpowers/specs/2026-09-19-central-rdc-pool-allocation-brd-fsd.md)** · **[.docx](docs/superpowers/specs/2026-09-19-central-rdc-pool-allocation-brd-fsd.docx)** — 46 tables, 47 sections, verified clean.

| Part | Sections | Content |
|---|---|---|
| **A — BRD** | A1-A10 | Problem (29/62 served, 46 pcs idle), objective, in/out scope, **your 3 decisions recorded as D1-D3**, 8 business rules (BR-RDC-01…08), quantified benefit, 7 risks with mitigations, assumptions, sign-off block |
| **B — FSD** | B1-B18 | Mode matrix, Part-by-Part processing sequence, 7 functional specs (FS-RDC-01…07), split-pass algorithm, data model, UI, reporting, **4 worked examples**, 6 invariants, edge cases, backward-compatibility fencing, impact map with line numbers, 8-point verification plan, 4-phase rollout, glossary, 4 open items |

**Two things I changed while writing it, both worth knowing:**

**1. Split rows go in a child table, not `ARS_ALLOC_WORKING`.** My earlier draft would have added a second row to the alloc table for a split line — that breaks the one-row-per-store-size grain that parking, Approve and alloc review depend on. The FSD now puts splits in a new `ARS_ALLOC_RDC_SPLIT` child table, with only `SRC_RDC` / `SRC_SPLIT_CNT` added to the alloc table. Logged as risk R6.

**2. I had the split ledger arithmetic wrong.** In my earlier chat messages the walk started from RDC-A for every store; it must start from *each store's own* RDC. Recomputed under the now-default `SINGLE_PREFERRED`, example E1 tags **A 14 / B 46**, not A 15 / B 45, and the split lands on HP04's L-line as `B2 + A4`. Related correction: `SPLIT_ALWAYS` and `SINGLE_PREFERRED` do **not** give identical per-RDC totals as I said earlier — both dispatch the full 24 pcs with one split line, but the totals shift by 1 piece depending on which line splits. E2 now shows all three policies side by side with this stated properly.

**On your "no issue in Own process" requirement** — §B13 gates all four changes on `rdc_mode == 'all'`, and invariant I-5 makes a row-for-row diff of a completed `Own` session against its parked snapshot a **blocking release gate**. Any difference at all counts as a defect.

The 2026-09-18 draft is marked superseded at the top; its `.docx` is now stale — tell me if you want both old files removed. Nothing committed to git yet.

Four open items for the business side are listed in §B18, the important one being **O1**: warehouse confirmation that picking can execute a two-source line. If they say no, the default flips from `SINGLE_PREFERRED` to `SINGLE_STRICT` and you accept occasional reduced lines.

content.text:
Cross needs more than "leave it alone" — I checked the code path and it has a structural defect.

## What Cross is supposed to do

> Take options **FROM** one RDC, send **TO** stores of another RDC.

## What the code actually does

Cross appears in exactly **two** places in [listing.py](backend/app/api/v1/endpoints/listing.py) — lines 1234-1236, and nowhere else:

```python
elif req.rdc_mode == "cross" and req.cross_from:
    stores_sql     = _stores_sql(req.cross_to)        # stores of the TO RDCs
    msa_rdc_filter = f" AND RDC IN ({cross_from})"    # options of the FROM RDCs
```

That filters the **option list** and `MSA_FNL_Q`. But `ARS_LISTING.RDC` is still stamped with the **store's own** RDC (Part 1 `S.[RDC]`, Part 2 `S.[RDC]` — no cross branch rewrites it).

Then the engine builds the size-level pool in [rule_engine_new.py:866-874](backend/app/services/rule_engine_new.py#L866-L874):

```sql
FROM [listed_table] L
INNER JOIN [ARS_MSA_VAR_ART] V
    ON  L.MAJ_CAT = V.MAJ_CAT ... AND L.CLR = V.CLR
    AND L.RDC = V.RDC              -- ← unconditional, no mode awareness
```

`msa_var_table` is the raw `ARS_MSA_VAR_ART` ([rule_engine_new.py:72](backend/app/services/rule_engine_new.py#L72)) — **no `cross_from` filter is applied anywhere in the engine**.

**Result: the option list comes from `cross_from`, but the stock the engine actually draws comes from the store's own RDC.** The two halves of Cross point at different warehouses.

### Example — Cross: FROM RDC-A → TO RDC-B stores

| Case | Option | A stock | B stock | Listing shows | Engine pool (`L.RDC = 'B'`) | Ships |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | X | 50 | **0** | `MSA_FNL_Q = 50` (A's) | B has no rows → **empty** | **0** |
| 2 | Y | 30 | 20 | `MSA_FNL_Q = 30` (A's) | B's 20 | **up to 20, from B** |

Case 1 is the whole point of Cross — A is overstocked, B's stores need it — and it ships nothing. Case 2 "works", but it draws from **B's own stock** while the screen quotes **A's 30**, so the listing figure is simply wrong.

Additionally, when `cross_from` names two or more RDCs, `MSA_FNL_Q` hits the same arbitrary-pick ambiguity as `All RDCs` (defect D-1 in the spec), because the RDC join predicate is added only for `own`.

This is read from the code, which is unambiguous on the join. The live consequence is expected but unmeasured — I can confirm it in minutes by checking a past cross-mode session for allocated rows.

## What this means for the design

My spec currently says "Cross unchanged". That would preserve a broken mode next to a newly correct one — and the two would visibly disagree.

| Option | What it means | Effort | Risk |
|---|---|---|---|
| **A. Leave Cross as-is** | Ship central pooling; Cross keeps its defect | none | Ops compares modes and finds Cross contradicts All RDCs; the defect stays live |
| **B. Fix Cross's pool source** *(recommended)* | Stage B's RDC join becomes mode-aware: under `cross` it matches `V.RDC IN (cross_from)` instead of the store's RDC. Also apply the `SUM`-across-RDCs fix so multi-`cross_from` is deterministic | small — the same mode-gate we're already adding for `All RDCs` | Changes Cross output, so it needs its own before/after review |
| **C. Retire Cross** | `All RDCs` + an optional "source only from RDC X" restriction reproduces Cross, per line rather than per run | medium | Removes a mode ops may still want for deliberate stock rebalancing |

**My recommendation: B now, C as a later simplification.**

B, because we are already making the pool build mode-aware for `All RDCs` — fixing Cross is the same edit with a different predicate, and leaving a known-defective branch adjacent to the new code is how defects get blamed on the new work.

C later, because central pooling makes Cross largely redundant: cross-shipping now happens **automatically, per line, only where it's needed** (example E1 line 7 — HP04 pulled from A without anyone selecting Cross). The one thing Cross would still uniquely offer is *deliberate* source restriction — "drain RDC-A into RDC-B's stores" for liquidation or rebalancing. Under the new design that's expressible as `All RDCs` with the split pass's preference order restricted to `cross_from`, which is a cleaner formulation of the same intent.

Note this also makes Cross's behavior **mode-gated and testable** the same way as the rest: invariant I-5 (row-for-row regression) protects `Own`, and Cross would get its own before/after comparison rather than a "must not change" gate, since B deliberately changes it.

## What I need from you

1. **A, B, or C** for Cross.
2. Want me to confirm the defect on a past cross-mode session first? Read-only query against `ARS_ALLOC_HISTORY` / `ARS_LISTING_SESSIONS` — I'd report how many cross runs exist and what they actually allocated.

Once you pick, I'll add a **§B13a — Cross RDC scope** section to the BRD/FSD (business impact, the fix, its own verification row in §B15, and a new open item), and regenerate the Word file.

# RDC scope with more than 2 warehouses

Right now you have 2 RDCs, so "the other one" is obvious. The moment you have 3, 4 or 10, *"the other one"* becomes *"which of the others, in what order, and how many may serve one line?"* — and every rule has to answer that. Here's how each of the three buttons behaves, in plain terms.

---

## 1. The simple mental model

Forget the button names for a moment. **Every allocation run is just two lists:**

| | Meaning |
|---|---|
| **SOURCE list** | Which warehouses' stock goes into the pot |
| **DESTINATION list** | Which stores get served from that pot |

The three buttons are just three presets of those two lists:

| Button | SOURCE list | DESTINATION list | Pot |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Own** (pick A, C) | A separately, C separately | stores of A, stores of C | **separate pots**, one per RDC |
| **All RDCs** | every RDC | every store | **one pot** |
| **Cross** (FROM A,C → TO B,D) | A + C | stores of B and D | **one pot** from A+C |

Once you see it this way, the answer to "how do we handle more RDCs" is: **the number of warehouses never changes the model — it only makes the lists longer.**

---

## 2. Own with 4 RDCs — no change needed

Say you have **A, B, C, D**. You select Own and tick **A and C**.

| Store | Tagged to | Can be served from | Pot |
|---|---|---|---|
| S1 | A | A only | A's pot |
| S3 | C | C only | C's pot |
| S2 | B | *(not in the run)* | — |
| S4 | D | *(not in the run)* | — |

It is simply **two independent allocations running in one pass**. Adding warehouses just adds more independent runs. Nothing about Own needs to change for N warehouses — it already works this way today, and it stays exactly as-is.

---

## 3. All RDCs with 4 warehouses

**Step 1 — one pot.** Add up all four:

| | A | B | C | D | **Pot** |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Size M stock | 4 | 0 | 9 | 2 | **15** |

**Step 2 — allocate** from 15, using today's rules. Say it gives:

| Store | Own warehouse | Gets |
|---|---|---|
| S1 | A | 6 |
| S2 | B | 5 |
| S3 | C | 4 |
| | | **15** |

**Step 3 — decide who ships each line.** This is where 4 warehouses differ from 2. With 2, "own first, then the other" is a complete instruction. With 4, after "own", you need an **order** for the remaining three. That order is one setting: a priority list, e.g. `A, B, C, D`.

Walking it (default policy = *single source preferred*):

| Store | Own | Needs | Order it tries | What it finds | Ships from |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| S1 | A | 6 | **A**, B, C, D | A has 4 (not enough alone), B has 0, **C has 9 ✓** | **C — 6** |
| S2 | B | 5 | **B**, A, C, D | B 0, A 4, C 3, D 2 — **none can cover 5 alone** → split: A 4 + C 1 | **A 4 + C 1** |
| S3 | C | 4 | **C**, A, B, D | C 2, A 0, B 0, D 2 — none alone → split: C 2 + D 2 | **C 2 + D 2** |

**Final picking list:**

| Warehouse | Ships | Had | Left |
|---|---|---|---|
| A | 4 | 4 | 0 |
| B | 0 | 0 | 0 |
| C | 9 | 9 | 0 |
| D | 2 | 2 | 0 |
| | **15** | 15 | 0 |

Every store got its full quantity, no warehouse was over-drawn. Notice S1, tagged to A, was served entirely by **C** — that's fine and automatic.

---

## 4. Cross with 4 warehouses

This is where it gets interesting, and where the current code genuinely can't cope.

**Example: Cross FROM `{A, C}` TO stores of `{B, D}`.** In plain words: *"empty out A and C into the stores of B and D."*

**Step 1 — the pot is A + C only** (B's and D's own stock is deliberately excluded):

| | A | C | **Pot** |
|---|---|---|---|
| Size M | 4 | 9 | **13** |

**Step 2 — allocate** to B-stores and D-stores from those 13:

| Store | Own warehouse | Gets |
|---|---|---|
| S2 | B | 5 |
| S4 | D | 6 |
| | | **11** (2 left over) |

**Step 3 — who ships?** Here's the crucial bit: **S2's own warehouse is B — and B is not a source.** So the rule "own warehouse first" has nothing to grab. The priority order does all the work:

| Store | Own | In source list? | Needs | Tries | Ships from |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| S2 | B | ❌ no | 5 | A (4, not enough), **C (9 ✓)** | **C — 5** |
| S4 | D | ❌ no | 6 | A (4), C (4) — neither alone | **A 4 + C 2** |

| Warehouse | Ships |
|---|---|
| A | 4 |
| C | 7 |
| | **11** |

**The point:** with 2 warehouses, Cross had only one possible source, so nobody had to decide anything. With 3+, Cross *must* have the same split pass that All RDCs uses — otherwise the system has no way to say which of A or C ships each line. **Cross and All RDCs stop being two different mechanisms and become the same mechanism with different source lists.**

And today's Cross can't do this at all: it filters the *option list* by the FROM warehouses, but the engine still draws stock from **the store's own warehouse** — which in this example holds nothing, because B and D were never meant to be sources. That's the defect I flagged, and with more than 2 warehouses it gets strictly worse.

---

## 5. Two new settings that 3+ warehouses force

### (a) The priority list becomes a real list

| Warehouses | Setting looks like | Why |
|---|---|---|
| 2 | "the other one" — no setting needed | only one possible answer |
| 4 | `A, B, C, D` — an ordered list | after "own", three candidates compete |

Simplest to maintain: one ordered list for the whole company. If you later want it per-region, you can add that — but don't start there.

### (b) A cap on how many warehouses may serve one line

With 2 warehouses, a split line means at most **2** pick documents. With 4, an unlucky line could be assembled from **4** warehouses — 4 picklists, 4 dispatches, for one store and one size:

| Store-size needing 8 pcs | A | B | C | D | Documents |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Uncapped split | 2 | 3 | 1 | 2 | **4** 😬 |
| Capped at 2 | 5 | — | 3 | — | **2** ✓ |

So a **maximum split count** (recommended default: **2**) is needed the day a third warehouse appears. Below the cap, the pass behaves as designed; at the cap, it takes the largest remaining sources and, if the line still can't be filled, treats it exactly like the strict-single-source case.

---

## 6. How the three split policies behave as warehouses multiply

| Policy | With 2 warehouses | With 4+ warehouses |
|---|---|---|
| **Split whenever short** | at most 2 sources per line | can fragment across **all** of them — needs the cap |
| **Single source preferred** *(default)* | splits only when neither can cover | **gets better** — more warehouses means a higher chance one of them can cover the whole line alone, so **fewer** splits |
| **Strict single source** | reduces the line when neither can cover | **also gets better** — more candidates, so fewer reductions |

Your chosen default (*single source preferred*) is the one that **improves** as you add warehouses. That's a good place to be.

---

## 7. What actually changes in the plan

| Area | 2 warehouses (current spec) | 3+ warehouses |
|---|---|---|
| Own | unchanged | **unchanged** — already works per-RDC |
| All RDCs | club all, own-first, then "the other" | club all, own-first, **then the priority list** |
| Cross | *(spec said: leave alone)* | **must use the same split pass**, with own-RDC excluded from sourcing |
| Priority setting | implicit | **ordered list of all warehouses** |
| Split cap | implicitly 2 | **explicit setting, default 2** |
| Split pass code | written for N warehouses already | **no change** — the loop walks a list, it never assumes 2 |
| API | `cross_from` / `cross_to` are already **lists** | **no change** — already N-ready |
| Data model | `SRC_RDC` per line | **no change** — one row per source RDC handles any N |

The good news: the design I wrote already loops over a **list** of warehouses rather than doing "A else B", so nothing structural breaks when a third appears. What genuinely needs adding is the two settings in §5 — and fixing Cross so it sources from the FROM list instead of the store's own warehouse.

---

## 8. What I'd recommend

1. **Treat all three buttons as one engine** with different source/destination lists. This is the single change that makes more warehouses a non-event.
2. **Fix Cross now** (option B from my last message), because at 3+ warehouses it's not a cosmetic defect — Cross simply cannot express its own purpose.
3. **Add the ordered priority list and the max-split cap (default 2)** to the spec now, even while you have 2 warehouses — they cost nothing today and save a redesign later.
4. **Keep "single source preferred" as the default** — it's the policy that gets better, not worse, as you grow.

Say the word and I'll fold all of this into the BRD/FSD — a new §B13a for Cross, the N-warehouse model in §B1, the two new settings in §B7, and these examples added to §B10 — then regenerate the Word file.

| Radio option | Value | Behaviour |
|---|---|---|
| Split whenever short | `SPLIT_ALWAYS` | Walk the preference order, take what each RDC has until the line is filled. Splits whenever the first RDC is short |
| **Single source preferred** *(default)* | `SINGLE_PREFERRED` | First pass: the first RDC in preference order that can cover the **whole** line takes it. Only if none can, fall back to the split walk |
| Strict single source | `SINGLE_STRICT` | Never split. If no RDC can cover the whole line, ship the largest single-RDC quantity available and **reduce the line** |

### B6.3.1 Maximum sources per line (`ALC_RDC_MAX_SPLIT`, default 2)

With two RDCs a split line means at most two pick documents. With three or more, an unconstrained
split walk could assemble one store-size from **every** warehouse — four picklists and four
dispatches for a single line. `ALC_RDC_MAX_SPLIT` bounds it.

| Value | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `1` | equivalent to `SINGLE_STRICT` — never more than one source |
| **`2`** *(default)* | at most two warehouses per line. **Cannot bind while only two RDCs exist** |
| `N` | at most N warehouses per line |

When the cap is reached and the line is still not filled, the remainder is handled exactly like
the `SINGLE_STRICT` shortfall (§B6.3.2): the line is reduced and stamped
`RDC_SPLIT_CAPPED(alloc=A,shipped=B)`. To maximise the fill achievable within the cap, the capped
walk orders candidates **own RDC first, then by availability descending** rather than by plain
priority order. Every capped line is counted and logged — the pass never truncates silently.

### B6.3.2 Algorithm

```
MAX_SPLIT = ALC_RDC_MAX_SPLIT                            # default 2

for each alloc line in (ST_RANK, alloc order):           # SHIP first, then HOLD
    remaining = qty
    order     = preference_order(store)                  # §B6.4 — own first, then priority list
    sources   = 0

    # pass 1 — whole-line cover (SINGLE_PREFERRED / SINGLE_STRICT only)
    if policy in (SINGLE_PREFERRED, SINGLE_STRICT):
        for rdc in order:
            if rdc_avail[rdc, option, size] >= remaining:
                emit(rdc, remaining); rdc_avail[rdc,…] -= remaining
                remaining = 0; sources = 1
                break

    # pass 2 — strict: one source only, reduce the rest
    if remaining > 0 and policy == SINGLE_STRICT:
        best = argmax(rdc_avail[rdc, option, size] for rdc in order)
        take = min(remaining, rdc_avail[best, option, size])
        emit(best, take); rdc_avail[best,…] -= take
        remaining -= take; sources = 1
        reduce_line(remaining, remark = 'RDC_SINGLE_SHORT'); remaining = 0

    # pass 3 — capped split walk
    if remaining > 0:
        candidates = own_rdc_first(order, then by rdc_avail desc)[:MAX_SPLIT]
        for rdc in candidates:
            take = min(remaining, rdc_avail[rdc, option, size])
            if take > 0:
                emit(rdc, take); rdc_avail[rdc,…] -= take
                remaining -= take; sources += 1
            if remaining == 0: break
        if remaining > 0:                                # cap bound before the line filled
            reduce_line(remaining, remark = 'RDC_SPLIT_CAPPED')
            remaining = 0

    assert remaining == 0                                # BR-RDC-03
    assert sources <= MAX_SPLIT                          # I-7
    assert all(v >= 0 for v in rdc_avail.values())       # BR-RDC-04
```

input.old_string:
**`SINGLE_STRICT` line reduction.** This is the only policy that can change an allocated
quantity, and it must stay internally consistent:

1. `SHIP_QTY` (or `HOLD_QTY`) on `ARS_ALLOC_WORKING` is reduced to the tagged quantity.
2. `ALLOC_REMARKS` gains `RDC_SINGLE_SHORT(alloc=A,shipped=B)`.
3. The option-grain `ALLOC_QTY` / `HOLD_QTY` rollup on `ARS_LISTING_WORKING` is refreshed, so
   Part 8.5 `OPT_STATUS` (which runs after parking) judges the real shipped quantity.
4. The un-tagged remainder stays unallocated and appears in the residual stock report.

Under `SPLIT_ALWAYS` and `SINGLE_PREFERRED` no quantity ever changes — the pass is pure tagging.

Two situations can reduce an allocated quantity — `SINGLE_STRICT` when no RDC covers the line,
and the `ALC_RDC_MAX_SPLIT` cap when it binds before the line is filled. Both must leave the
data internally consistent:

1. `SHIP_QTY` (or `HOLD_QTY`) on `ARS_ALLOC_WORKING` is reduced to the tagged quantity.
2. `ALLOC_REMARKS` gains `RDC_SINGLE_SHORT(alloc=A,shipped=B)` or

   Part 8.5 `OPT_STATUS` (which runs after parking) judges the real shipped quantity.
4. The un-tagged remainder stays unallocated and appears in the residual stock report.
5. The run log and the cockpit report the count and quantity of reduced lines — **never a silent
   truncation**.

Under `SPLIT_ALWAYS` and `SINGLE_PREFERRED` with the cap unbound, **no quantity ever changes** —
the pass is pure tagging. With only two RDCs in operation, a cap of 2 can never bind, so the
default configuration is pure tagging.

```

└─────────────────────────────────────┘  └─────────────────────────────────────┘
```

|---|---|---|

│  Split lines             38  of 8,421   (0.5%)                           │

│  Untagged sourced     2,180 pcs by priority                              │
│                                                      [ Export picklist ] │
└──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
```

Those five figures are what tell ops whether clubbing is working: how much moved between
warehouses, how often a line had to split, whether any line was reduced, and how much was routed
by fallback rather than by tag.

flow into the existing `ARS_RUN_PARAMS_AUDIT` capture and appear automatically in the Compare and
Trends views.

## 1. New setting — `ALC_RDC_MAX_SPLIT` (default 2) · §B6.3.1

Caps how many warehouses may serve one store-size line.

| Value | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `1` | equivalent to `SINGLE_STRICT` |
| **`2`** *(default)* | **cannot bind while only two RDCs exist** — so today's config stays pure tagging |
| `N` | at most N warehouses per line |

When the cap binds before a line is filled, the remainder is reduced and stamped
`RDC_SPLIT_CAPPED(alloc=A,shipped=B)` — same treatment as the `SINGLE_STRICT` shortfall. To get the best fill within the cap, the capped walk orders candidates **own RDC first, then by availability descending** rather than plain priority.

## 2. `ALC_RDC_PRIORITY` is now an ordered list of *every* RDC · §B6.4

`"A,B"` today, `"A,B,C,D"` when warehouses are added — not a pair. With two RDCs the order after "own" is forced and barely matters; from three onward it decides most cross-ship routing. **An RDC missing from the list is appended alphabetically**, so a newly created warehouse can never be silently excluded from sourcing.

## 3. §B8 rewritten as the Option 1 UI spec

Progressive disclosure — the sourcing panel appears only under `All RDCs`:

| Sub-section | Content |
|---|---|
| B8.1 | `Own` selected — today's screen plus the untagged warning |

| Where | Change |
|---|---|
| §A6 | **BR-RDC-09** (cap) and **BR-RDC-10** (no silent truncation) — now 10 business rules |
| §B6.3.2 | Algorithm rewritten with the three passes and both assertions |

import re
import sys

from docx import Document
from docx.enum.table import WD_TABLE_ALIGNMENT
from docx.enum.text import WD_ALIGN_PARAGRAPH
from docx.oxml import OxmlElement
from docx.oxml.ns import qn
from docx.shared import Inches, Pt, RGBColor

SRC, DST = sys.argv[1], sys.argv[2]

    el = OxmlElement('w:shd')
    el.set(qn('w:val'), 'clear')

    cell._tc.get_or_add_tcPr().append(el)


def add_inline(par, text, size=None, bold=False):
    """Render one line of markdown inline markup into runs."""
    for tok in INLINE.split(text):
        if not tok:
            continue
        run = par.add_run()
        if tok.startswith('***') and tok.endswith('***'):
            run.text, run.bold, run.italic = tok[3:-3], True, True
        elif tok.startswith('**') and tok.endswith('**'):
            run.text, run.bold = tok[2:-2], True
        elif tok.startswith('`') and tok.endswith('`'):
            run.text = tok[1:-1]
            run.font.name = 'Consolas'
            run.font.color.rgb = RGBColor(0xA3, 0x1A, 0x1A)
        elif tok.startswith('*') and tok.endswith('*'):
            run.text, run.italic = tok[1:-1], True
        else:
            run.text = tok
        if bold:
            run.bold = True
        if size:

    return par


def is_table_sep(line):
    s = line.strip()
    return bool(s.startswith('|') and re.fullmatch(r'[\|\s:\-]+', s)) and '-' in s

            run = par.add_run('\n'.join(code_buf))
            run.font.name = 'Consolas'

            shade_p = OxmlElement('w:shd')

    if in_code:

        table.autofit = True

            cell = table.rows[0].cells[c]

            add_inline(cell.paragraphs[0], txt, size=8.5, bold=True)

        for row in body:
            cells = table.add_row().cells
            for c in range(ncols):

                cells[c].text = ''

        for r in table.rows:
            for cell in r.cells:

    m = re.match(r'^(#{1,6})\s+(.*)$', stripped)
    if m:

        add_inline(par, m.group(2))
        for run in par.runs:

        pbdr = OxmlElement('w:pBdr')

        bottom.set(qn('w:sz'), '6')
        bottom.set(qn('w:color'), 'C0C6D0')

        par._p.get_or_add_pPr().append(pbdr)

        continue

    if stripped.startswith('> '):

        par.paragraph_format.left_indent = Inches(0.3)
        add_inline(par, stripped[2:])
        for run in par.runs:
            run.italic = True
            run.font.color.rgb = MUTED
        i += 1
        continue

    # lists
    m = re.match(r'^(\d+)\.\s+(.*)$', stripped)
    if m:
        add_inline(doc.add_paragraph(style='List Number'), m.group(2))
        i += 1
        continue
    if re.match(r'^[-*]\s+', stripped):
        add_inline(doc.add_paragraph(style='List Bullet'), re.sub(r'^[-*]\s+', '', stripped))
        i += 1
        continue

    buf = [stripped]
    j = i + 1

Measured diff between the two:

| | v1.0 (19 Sep) | v1.1 (21 Sep) | Δ |
|---|---|---|---|
| Sections | 47 | 55 | **+8** |
| Tables | 46 | 47 | +1 |
| Words | 5,414 | 6,500 | **+1,086 (+20 %)** |
| Sections removed | — | — | **0** |

**Nothing was removed or reversed.** v1.0's three approved decisions (D1 three policies / Policy 2 default, D2 one ledger, D3 tag stays authoritative) are unchanged in v1.1. The difference is two things v1.0 didn't cover.

## 1. Multi-RDC handling — what happens when you add a 3rd or 4th warehouse

v1.0 was written for your two RDCs. It worked, but two settings only become meaningful at 3+, and they weren't specified:

| New in v1.1 | What it does |
|---|---|
| **§B6.3.1 — `ALC_RDC_MAX_SPLIT`** (default 2) | Caps how many warehouses may serve one store-size line. Without it, a 4-RDC setup could assemble one line from 4 warehouses = 4 picklists |
| **§B6.3.2 — Algorithm** | Rewritten as three explicit passes (whole-line cover → strict → capped split walk) with the cap and its assertions |
| **§B6.3.3 — Line reduction** | Was a paragraph covering only `SINGLE_STRICT`; now a section covering **both** reduction causes, with 5 required consistency steps |
| **§B6.4 — priority as an ordered list** | `ALC_RDC_PRIORITY` is now an ordered list naming *every* RDC (`"A,B,C,D"`), with an append rule so a new warehouse can never be silently excluded |
| **BR-RDC-09, BR-RDC-10** | Cap rule; no-silent-truncation rule (8 → 10 business rules) |
| **I-7, I-8** | Sources ≤ cap; every reduction stamped and counted (6 → 8 invariants) |
| **V9, V10** | Cap fires correctly at N=4 (blocking); cap cannot bind at N=2 (8 → 10 checks) |
| **O2a** | Confirm the cap default before a 3rd RDC goes live; O2 reworded for the ordered list |

Important: with your **current two RDCs, a cap of 2 can never bind** — so v1.1 changes nothing about how today's runs would behave. It just means no redesign when a third warehouse arrives.

## 2. Full UI specification (§B8)

v1.0 had a 4-item bullet list describing the controls in prose. v1.1 has **five sub-sections with actual mockups**:

| | v1.0 | v1.1 |
|---|---|---|
| `Own` screen | not shown | B8.1 — mockup |
| `All RDCs` screen | not shown | B8.2 — mockup with the RDC SOURCING panel |
| Control spec | 4 bullets | B8.3 — table: policy radios, drag-to-reorder priority chips, max-split select, live pool summary, untagged banner |
| Post-run results | **absent** | B8.4 — new `RDC SPLIT` results block (pick by RDC, cross-shipped, split lines, reduced lines, untagged sourced) |
| Run Parameters | one line | B8.5 |

B8.4 is the genuinely new idea — v1.0 specified how to *configure* the split but never how you'd *see what it did* after the run.

## 3. One formatting fix

List items count went 29 → 24, which looks like content loss but isn't: my converter was splitting any list item that wrapped across two source lines into two paragraphs — breaking bold across the boundary and losing the indent. Those 5 orphan fragments are now merged back into their parent items. Affects §A2, §B6.3.3 and §B8.

## Unchanged between the two

Everything else: the BRD problem statement and 29→60 benefit case, all three decisions, the four functional changes (FS-RDC-01 to 04), the child-table data model, all four worked examples with their arithmetic, the impact map, the `Own`/`Cross` protection and its row-for-row release gate, and the rollout plan.

**Short version:** v1.0 = the approved design for 2 RDCs. v1.1 = the same design, future-proofed for N RDCs and with the screen fully specified.
is this "priority as an ordered list" maintain store wise or gloable?

**Global — one ordered list for the whole system.** There is no per-store priority column.

But per-store *behaviour* still emerges, because the store's own RDC is always promoted to the front of that global list:

**Global setting:** `ALC_RDC_PRIORITY = "A,B,C,D"` (one value, maintained once)

| Store | Its tag | Effective order for that store | Comes from |
|---|---|---|---|
| S1 | `C` | **C**, A, B, D | own first, then the global list minus C |
| S2 | `B` | **B**, A, C, D | same |
| S3 | `A` | **A**, B, C, D | same |
| S4 | *(blank)* | A, B, C, D | global list as-is |

So four stores get four different effective orders from **one** maintained value. You get per-store routing without per-store maintenance.

## Where it lives

| | |
|---|---|
| Stored in | `ARS_BUSINESS_RULES` as `ALC_RDC_PRIORITY` |
| Edited at | Settings → Business Rules (SUPER_ADMIN only, every change audited) |
| If inactive/unset | falls to tier 3 — largest-available-first, per line |
| New RDC not in the list | appended alphabetically, never silently excluded |

## Why not per-store

The earlier draft had a 4th tier: an `RDC_PRIORITY` column on the store master, per store. I dropped it in the final spec (§B6.4) — it meant **451 rows of new master data to curate** with no demonstrated need, and the own-RDC-first rule already covers the ordinary case.

## The honest limitation

A single global list assumes the "second-best" warehouse is the same for everyone. That is:

| Situation | Is a global list right? |
|---|---|
| **2 RDCs (today)** | **Yes, completely** — after "own", there is only one other choice. The setting barely does anything |
| 3-4 RDCs, similar freight cost | Yes, good enough |
| 3+ RDCs spread geographically | **No** — a Delhi store's second-best is not a Chennai store's second-best |

| Own RDC | Then try |
|---|---|
| A | B, C, D |
| B | A, D, C |
| C | D, A, B |
| D | C, B, A |

Four rows for four warehouses, and it captures the geography properly. It slots in as a tier between the current tier 1 and tier 2 without changing anything else in the design — the pass just calls `preference_order(store)` and doesn't care where the list came from.

Added. **[v1.2 Word file](docs/superpowers/specs/2026-09-21-central-rdc-pool-allocation-brd-fsd-v1.2.docx)** — 49 tables, 57 sections, 0 broken cross-references.

## What the per-RDC fallback order is

One ordered list **per warehouse**, answering *"if a store's own warehouse is X and X is short, which warehouse next?"*

| Own RDC | Then try | Effective order for a store tagged there |
|---|---|---|
| A | B, C, D | A, B, C, D |
| B | A, D, C | B, A, D, C |
| C | D, A, B | C, D, A, B |
| D | C, B, A | D, C, B, A |

**4 rows for 4 warehouses** — versus 451 rows for a per-store column. It captures the geography (a Delhi store's second-best isn't a Chennai store's second-best) at 1 % of the maintenance cost.

## Where it sits in the chain (§B6.4)

Tier numbering is unchanged — the map is a *modifier inside tier 1*, because it's keyed on the store's **own** RDC:

| Tier | Order | `PREF_TIER` |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | own RDC first, then **per-RDC map** if defined | `1F` |
| 1 | own RDC first, then **global list** | `1` |
| 2 | global list alone (untagged store) | `2` |
| 3 | largest-available-first | `3` |

`PREF_TIER` changed from `TINYINT` to `NVARCHAR(2)` to carry `1F`, so you can measure exactly how many lines the map actually routed.

## It's a preference, never a filter

Four safety rules so a partial or stale map can't strand stock:

| Situation | Behaviour |
|---|---|
| An RDC missing from a list | appended — by global order, then alphabetically |
| No entry for a store's own RDC | that store uses the global list (`PREF_TIER='1'`); others unaffected |
| A decommissioned RDC named in the map | ignored — holds no stock, walk moves on |
| Untagged stores | unaffected — nothing to key on, they resolve at tier 2 |

## Where it's configured

Settings → **Business Rules** as `ALC_RDC_FALLBACK_ORDER`, JSON keyed by own RDC, SUPER_ADMIN-gated with the registry's change audit. **Not** a cockpit control — it's standing configuration, not a per-run decision. When it's active, the cockpit's priority chips go read-only with *"overridden per RDC — see Business Rules"*.

## Recommended setting today

**Leave it unset.** With two warehouses, "own first, then the other one" is fully determined — the map can express nothing the own-first rule doesn't already give you. Set `ALC_RDC_PRIORITY = "A,B"` and populate the map the day a third RDC goes live. That's recorded as open item **O2b**, and verification **V11** proves an unset map reproduces the baseline output exactly.

Also added: 4 new edge-case rows (§B12), V11 as a blocking check (§B15), and the registry entry (§B7).

aiTitle: Redesign stock allocation across multiple RDCs

content.text:
Grounded in your actual data:

| Fact | Value |
|---|---|
| Stores | **521** |
| RDCs | **DW01** (284 stores) · **DH24** (237) |
| Untagged stores | **0** — the master is fully tagged |
| Hierarchy | RDC → **HUB** → store; 110 hubs, **none spanning two RDCs** |
| Hub shape | 21 real hubs covering ~432 stores (10-30 each) + 89 single-store hubs |
| Precedent for a maintained column | `MANUAL_ST_PRIORITY` already sits on the store master |
| Caution | the master carries `UPLOAD_DATETIME` — it is an **uploaded** table |

Two things jump out. **You have zero untagged stores**, so the whole fallback discussion is insurance, not a live problem. And **HUB already is the logistics layer** between RDC and store — which is almost certainly the right grain, not the store.

## The honest starting point

With **2 RDCs, a per-store priority can express nothing.** Own first, then the only other one — the order is fully determined for all 521 stores. Any table you build today would be 521 rows that change no allocation. This becomes real only at 3+ RDCs.

So the question is really *"where should it live when we need it?"* — design the hook now, don't populate it.

## Three candidate homes

| | Where | Grain | Rows to maintain | Survives master re-upload | Queryable |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| **A** | new `RDC_PRIORITY` column on `Master_ALC_INPUT_ST_MASTER` | store | **521** | ⚠️ at risk | ✗ delimited string |
| **B** | new table `ARS_STORE_RDC_PRIORITY` | store **and** hub | **21** (+ exceptions) | ✅ | ✅ |
| **C** | `ALC_RDC_FALLBACK_ORDER` business rule *(already in the spec)* | RDC | **2-4** | ✅ | ✅ |

### Why not A

- The master is **uploaded**. A manually curated column can be wiped by the next refresh. `MANUAL_ST_PRIORITY` already lives with that exposure — worth confirming how your upload handles it before adding a second one.
- A delimited string like `"DH24,DW01"` in one column can't be validated, can't answer *"which stores route to DH24 second?"*, and can't be diffed.
- It contradicts the codebase's own pattern — `facons_mbq_service` states master attributes are *"joined LIVE at read time… never copied"*.

A is defensible purely on consistency with `MANUAL_ST_PRIORITY`. But it's the weakest of the three.

### Recommended: B, keyed at HUB with a store-level override

```
ARS_STORE_RDC_PRIORITY
┌─────────────┬───────────────┬──────────────────────────────────────────┐
│ SCOPE       │ NVARCHAR(10)  │ 'HUB' or 'STORE'                         │
│ SCOPE_CD    │ NVARCHAR(20)  │ HUB code, or ST_CD for an exception      │
│ SEQ         │ INT           │ 1, 2, 3 … the order                      │
│ RDC         │ NVARCHAR(20)  │ the warehouse at that position           │
│ IS_ACTIVE   │ BIT           │                                          │
│ UPDATED_BY  │ NVARCHAR(50)  │ audit                                    │
│ UPDATED_AT  │ DATETIME      │ audit                                    │
└─────────────┴───────────────┴──────────────────────────────────────────┘
PK (SCOPE, SCOPE_CD, SEQ)   ·   UNIQUE (SCOPE, SCOPE_CD, RDC)
```

**Why HUB is the right grain for you:** 21 hub rows cover 432 stores, and stores in one hub share a truck — they physically cannot have different sourcing preferences. The 89 single-store hubs are already store-grain, so one table handles both without a second concept. And no hub spans two RDCs, so a hub's order is always well-defined.

One row per position (not a delimited string) means it's queryable, validatable, editable in a grid, and a partial list is legal — missing RDCs just append.

**Maintenance:** a small grid page under Data Management, same pattern as the existing store-master table view, plus an Excel bulk upload like the Facons modules. Realistically ~21 rows edited when a warehouse opens or a hub moves — not routine work.

### Resulting resolution chain (extends §B6.4)

| Order | Source | `PREF_TIER` | Rows |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Store's **own RDC** always first | — | from tag |
| 2 | `ARS_STORE_RDC_PRIORITY` **STORE** row | `1S` | exceptions only |
| 3 | `ARS_STORE_RDC_PRIORITY` **HUB** row | `1H` | ~21 |
| 4 | `ALC_RDC_FALLBACK_ORDER` per-RDC map | `1F` | 2-4 |
| 5 | `ALC_RDC_PRIORITY` global list | `1` / `2` | 1 |
| 6 | Largest-available-first | `3` | 0 |

Each tier is optional and empty by default, so today's behaviour is unchanged and every level you populate later narrows the routing without touching code — the pass only calls `preference_order(store)`.

## My recommendation

**Don't build B now.** Ship what's already specced — the per-RDC map (2-4 rows) plus the global list — and record `ARS_STORE_RDC_PRIORITY` in the FSD as the **documented extension point** with this exact schema and its place in the chain. When the third RDC arrives, you add the table and populate ~21 hub rows; nothing else moves.

Two things I'd do regardless:

1. **Check how your store-master upload treats `MANUAL_ST_PRIORITY`** — if a refresh wipes it, that's a live bug affecting store ranking today, independent of this work. I can verify it in a few minutes.
2. Note in the spec that **HUB**, not store, is the natural grain — it's the insight that turns 521 rows of maintenance into 21.

Want me to add §B6.4.3 with the `ARS_STORE_RDC_PRIORITY` schema and the six-tier chain as a specified-but-not-built extension, and rebuild as v1.3?

This conversation is already on disk:

Sessions are stored per **project folder path**, not per client. The desktop app, the CLI and this VS Code extension all read the same directory. So:

1. Open the Claude Code desktop app on **this same machine, as this same Windows user**
2. Open the folder `d:\projects\ars_prod`
3. Use `/resume` and pick this session — it's the one modified today — or `--continue` to pick up the most recent one automatically

Conditions that must hold: same machine, same user profile, same project path (the folder name `d--projects-ars-prod` is derived from `d:\projects\ars_prod`). Claude Code transcripts are **local, not cloud-synced** — open the desktop app on your laptop instead and this history won't be there.

I'd also close the session here before resuming elsewhere, rather than running both against the same transcript.

That's a separate product with its own history. It can't resume a Claude Code session, and it won't know anything about this conversation. It does have your Universal MCP server configured (per `CLAUDE.md`), so it can query live ARS data — but it would be starting cold on this design.
